solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Islander takes my vessel round island on return

indicators.note: the two outer pieces go round, so they enclose what follows

parts.note: 'Cor!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'
a can is a vessel for holding liquid

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for island is read backwards

explanation.surface: An islander sails home, taking a personal boat around an island on the return voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is not a possessive here but the exclamation 'Cor!'; 'on return' reverses the island abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Corsican is a native of Corsica, the Mediterranean island belonging to France.

clue.text: Buffalo Bill entertains me — funny stuff

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: Buffalo Bill was the nickname of William Cody, the Wild West showman

explanation.surface: The Wild West showman puts on an act for the speaker, which proves amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy is entertainment meant to make people laugh, so it is funny material.

clue.text: Robber in Austria captured by someone on horseback

indicators.note: being captured means being held inside the captor, so this letter goes within the next piece

parts.note: a rider is someone sitting on a horse
A is the international vehicle registration letter for Austria

explanation.surface: A thief in Austria is caught by a mounted policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider attacks to seize goods, so he is a kind of robber or plunderer.

clue.text: One cold beginning to trouble you and me — sudden occurrence

parts.note: the Roman numeral I means one
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of trouble is used

parts.note: us means you and me together

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a cold starting is trouble for both of us, arriving all at once.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine an ictus is a sudden attack such as a stroke or seizure, an abrupt event.

clue.text: Beautiful female in song — finale coming up

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: the finale is the end

explanation.surface: An opera aria about a lovely woman nears its finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' reverses END to DNE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariadne is the Cretan princess of Greek myth who helped Theseus, celebrated for her beauty.

clue.text: Is troublesome holy book revolting?

parts.note: Acts (of the Apostles) is a book of the New Testament
a people up in arms are up, in revolt

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a scripture causes trouble by being disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' suggests disgusting, but here it means rising up.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave or malfunction, causing bother for others.

clue.text: Mostly crude actor playing a king?

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved around in a new arrangement
mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A coarse actor takes on the role of a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' leaves CRUD, and 'playing' shuffles CRUD with ACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A court card is a picture card in a pack: king, queen or jack; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: City beach maybe that is found on travel

parts.note: sand is what a beach is made of, an example
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A beach town that people discover on their travels.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a large city on the Pacific coast of California.

clue.text: Superlative advice telling prying person to ease up

definitions.text: advice telling prying person to ease up
definitions.meaning: split as two words it tells a snoop to look closely less often

explanation.surface: Top-notch counsel to a nosy neighbour to stop snooping.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless describes something with no equal, unrivalled; read as two words it urges looking less.

clue.text: Keep isn't protected by chief

indicators.note: something protected is held safe inside, so this goes within the other piece

parts.note: main means chief or principal
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: The castle keep is unguarded by the leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a castle tower but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to keep it going or keep it in good condition.

clue.text: Fruit one of five children brought to church

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five born together
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A quintuplet arrives at church with a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The quince is a hard, pear-shaped fruit used for jelly and jam.

clue.text: Manage first to last to create an international sales organisation

indicators.note: the first letter is sent to the end of the word, moving it to last place

parts.note: to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: An instruction to run something from start to finish to build a global trading body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the C of COPE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: OPEC, the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, coordinates its members' oil sales.

clue.text: In smart clothes that's embroidered

definitions.meaning: a story ... has been embellished or made to seem better

explanation.surface: Someone well turned out in an embroidered garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed up means formally attired, and figuratively embellished, as a tale with added detail.

clue.text: Ordeal coming with industrialisation

indicators.note: the answer comes within the next word, sitting inside its letters

explanation.surface: Hardship arriving alongside the factory age.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a painful test of endurance, an ordeal.

clue.text: Effected reforms — this to become dame?

parts.note: read as an instruction, the first word of the answer is rearranged to spell the clue's dame

explanation.surface: Reforms were carried out: could this turn someone into a dame?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: MADE, with its letters changed, becomes DAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Made changes means brought about alterations, which is what effecting reforms is.

clue.text: Man will come in a taxi having wandered around and about — that's self-evident

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so these letters go inside the others
letters that wander around end up in a new order

parts.note: IOM is the Isle of Man
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A man boards a taxi that has been driving aimlessly, which is plainly obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, a British crown dependency; 'having wandered around' gives XATI, and 'will come in' places the island inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Axiomatic describes something taken as true without proof, obviously so.

clue.text: See 14
Fat little son weeps

parts.note: blubber is whale fat
S is the short form of son

explanation.surface: A chubby small boy is crying.
explanation.definitionFit: To blubber is to cry noisily, so a person who blubbers weeps.

clue.text: Fliers going up over Surrey town area to give final message

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, are fliers
Ewell is a town in Surrey, part of the borough of Epsom and Ewell

explanation.surface: Planes rise above a Surrey town to send a parting signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns RAF into FAR; 'over' places it above EWELL in this down entry. Surrey is a county south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell is a goodbye, the last thing said on parting.

clue.text: Pat may be such an important person in pathology

definitions.text: Pat may be such an important person in pathology

parts.words: Pat may be such an important person in pathology
parts.note: Pat is a woman's name, and it heads the word pathology, so that woman stands first in it

explanation.surface: A senior figure in medical pathology could be someone called Pat.
explanation.walkthrough: PAT opens the word 'pathology': a lady leading it. The answer also means a star actress.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading lady is the principal female role in a play or film, an important person.

clue.text: Pains — they ultimately must get tackled by doctors

indicators.note: being tackled means being grabbed and held, so this goes inside the other piece

parts.note: GPs are general practitioners, family doctors

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of they is used

explanation.surface: Aches that, in the end, the doctors must deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyp is British slang for pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'.

clue.text: See 19
Follower of reformer to lie around on a road

parts.note: to loll is to lie about lazily

explanation.surface: A disciple of a reformer lounging about on a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Lollards were followers of John Wycliffe, the 14th-century English church reformer.

clue.text: Female singer (51) in religious festival

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female opera singer
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A female vocalist aged 51 performs at a religious festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Divali, also Diwali, is the Hindu festival of lights.

clue.text: Woman housing old lover in building's extension?

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it inside, so this goes within the name

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A woman puts up her former partner in the house's add-on.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extra building or wing added to a main building.

clue.text: Smile when crossing river — fish is seen

indicators.note: to cross something is to go across it, so the smile straddles this letter

parts.note: to beam is to smile broadly

explanation.surface: Someone grins while crossing a river and spotting a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The bream is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Like architectural style of a pillar and somehow not right

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some new order
not tells us to leave this letter out of the pillar

explanation.surface: Something resembling a pillar's architectural style, but slightly off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' removes R from PILLAR, leaving PILLA, and the final adverb mixes A PILLA AND into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Palladian is the classical building style derived from the architect Andrea Palladio.

clue.text: Breton doctor taken in by Scottish one?

indicators.note: being taken in means being placed inside, so this goes within the next piece

parts.note: ane is the Scots word for one

explanation.surface: A doctor from Brittany is fooled by a Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: A Breton is from Brittany in France; André is a typical French man's name, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: André is a common French first name, which a man from Brittany might bear.

clue.text: Well-balanced sides in tremendous competitions

parts.note: even means level, well balanced

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Evenly matched teams in thrilling contests.
explanation.definitionFit: Events are the separate contests at a sports meeting, competitions.

clue.text: Rush around ward in a frenzy to provide equipment

indicators.note: around means one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to hare is to rush

indicators.note: a frenzy is wild disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dashes frantically about a hospital ward to fetch equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like the verb of the dash, but it supplies a synonym; 'in a frenzy' scrambles WARD to RDWA.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardware means tools and equipment, or the physical parts of a computer.

clue.text: Comfort found in the sun — wonderful!

parts.note: Sol is the sun, from Latin
ace is slang for excellent, wonderful

explanation.surface: Someone finds relief basking in the sunshine and calls it great.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation in distress, comfort.

clue.text: I have a meal about nine, ending with coffee — it's an obsession

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the meal is read backwards

parts.note: a feed is a meal
IX is nine in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is taken from coffee

explanation.surface: Someone always eats around nine and finishes with coffee: a fixed habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses FEED to DEEF. Idée fixe is French for a fixed idea.
explanation.definitionFit: An idée fixe is a fixed idea that dominates the mind, an obsession.
